headline: Approved Assembly Square and East Somerville tax increment financing zone; ordained homeless shelter zoning amendment; approved $332,497 Tufts Street soil fund.
summary: The council approved a tax increment financing zone for Assembly Square and East Somerville and a zoning change on homeless shelters. It approved several grants and fund transfers and referred many zoning and funding items to committees. Councilors Ewen-Campen and Scott announced resignations effective December 31, 2026.
decisions: Approved resolution recognizing the seriousness of myotonic dystrophy and supporting September 15 as International Myotonic Dystrophy Awareness Day.
Approved resolution in support of striking Encore Boston Harbor workers.
Approved and sent for discussion a resolution asking the Director of Engineering and Commissioner of Public Works to review street restoration requirements after utility excavations.
Approved and sent for discussion a resolution asking about a street preservation offset fee for utility excavations.
Approved and sent for discussion a resolution asking how the City sets, monitors, and enforces construction timelines for municipal projects.
Approved and sent for discussion a resolution asking officials to review best practices for timely completion of public construction projects.
Approved Finance Committee report on grants, fund transfers, fund appropriations, a prior year invoice, and a stabilization fund.
Approved acceptance and expenditure of a $65,000 grant from the Mass Department of Mental Health to the Police Department.
Approved acceptance and expenditure of a $12,000 grant from the Mass Department of Mental Health to the Police Department.
Approved transfer of $315,000 from the Sewer Enterprise Debt Service Account to the Morrison Avenue & Greater Davis Square Area Sewer Separation Design Capital Fund.
Approved use of $8,800 in Police Salaries funds for Fiscal Year 2027 cost of living increases for the Deputy Chief positions.
Approved acceptance and expenditure of a $284,700 grant from the Massachusetts Gaming Commission for the Eastern Washington Street Transit Priority Project.
Approved payment of a prior year invoice totaling $3,572 for the ArcGIS Urban module.
Approved acceptance and expenditure of an $85,933.60 grant from the Boston Region Metropolitan Planning Organization for Bluebikes equipment replacement.
Approved acceptance and expenditure of a $366,729.25 grant from the Metropolitan Area Planning Council for Bluebikes e-bikes, batteries, and docking stations.
Approved creation of the Tufts Street Soil Project Stabilization Fund and acceptance of a $332,497 payment from Unifirst Corporation; vote was 10 aye, with Councilor Strezo absent.
Approved appropriation of $332,497 from the Tufts Street Soil Project Stabilization Fund for remediation at 50 Tufts Street; vote was 10 aye, with Councilor Strezo absent.
Approved acceptance and expenditure of a $187,200.00 Municipal Vulnerability Preparedness Grant for the Green and Cool Somerville sidewalk and tree project.
Approved acceptance and expenditure of a $20,239 grant from the United States Bureau of Justice Assistance for Police Department overtime related to the 2026 World Cup.
Approved transfer of $60,000 from the DPW-Admin Salaries & Wages Temp Account to the DPW-Admin Professional & Technical Services Account for temporary clerical staffing.
Approved Land Use Committee report on the Urban Center Housing Tax Increment Financing zone and an amendment on homeless shelters.
Approved the Urban Center Housing Tax Increment Financing (UCH-TIF) Zone, Plan, and Form of Agreement for Assembly Square and East Somerville; vote was 10 aye, with Councilor Strezo absent.
Ordained, as amended, the amendment to Section 2.1.1 of the Zoning Ordinance regarding Homeless Shelters; vote was 10 aye, with Councilor Strezo absent.
Approved School Building Facilities and Maintenance Committee report on custodial staffing, rodent control, temperature control, Winter Hill School, Cummings School, and a teen center.
Marked the resolution on a teen center at the Cummings School as work completed.
Marked the order on custodial staffing at the East Somerville Community School as work completed.
Marked the resolution thanking city departments for work on rodent issues at the West Somerville Neighborhood School as work completed.
Referred the amendment to Sections 3.2.17 and other sections of the Zoning Ordinance on parking maximums to the Land Use Committee for recommendation.
Referred the amendment to Zoning Ordinance ground story elevation requirements to the Land Use Committee for recommendation.
Referred the amendment to streamline the jurisdiction of review boards to the Land Use Committee for recommendation.
Referred the amendment to align with State Law on protected accessory dwelling units to the Land Use Committee for recommendation.
Referred the amendment to clarify requirements for principal entrances to the Land Use Committee for recommendation.
Referred the amendment to update terminology for affordable dwelling units and commercial spaces to the Land Use Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to appropriate $350,000 from the Immigrant Legal Services Stabilization Fund to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to appropriate $255,045 for Fiscal Year 2027 Vision Zero efforts to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to accept and expend a $295,463 State 911 grant to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to accept and expend a $215,919.15 grant to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to accept and expend a $159,754.04 grant to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to accept and expend a $24,500 grant to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to accept and expend a $9,809.81 grant that requires a match to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to pay prior year invoices totaling $80,852.95 to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Approved payment of prior year invoices totaling $1,687.50 for medical screening services.
Approved payment of a prior year invoice totaling $19.76 for phone interpretation services.
Item 7.18 was withdrawn.
Referred the amendment to Section 3.1.7.c of the Zoning Ordinance to the Land Use Committee for recommendation.
Referred the request to enter lease agreements for commercial arts space at the Somerville Armory Building, 191 Highland Avenue, to the Finance Committee for recommendation.
Approved the 9/11 Remembrance Ceremony public event license for Veteran Services.
Approved Junkyard LLC public event license for Junkyard Davis Square on September 19.
Approved new Drainlayer's License for Knight Excavation Co. Inc.
Approved new Second Hand Dealer License for The Heartland Roadshow, 30 Washington Street.
Approved, by motion to approve them this evening, public event licenses and other licenses for items 9.1 through 9.10.
Referred the Public Communication from Marianne Walles on Zoning Ordinance comments to the Land Use Committee.
Councilor Ewen-Campen's resignation from the City Council, effective December 31, 2026, was placed on file.
Councilor Scott's resignation from the City Council, effective December 31, 2026, was placed on file.
Placed on file and sent for discussion the report on the Cummings School winter warming center after action report and improvement plan.

# City of Somerville, Massachusetts · City Council · Meeting Minutes

Thursday, September 10, 2026 · 7:00 PM

NOTICE: This is NOT the official version of the City Council's minutes. While reasonable efforts have · been made to assure the accuracy of the data provided, do not rely on this information without first · checking with the City Clerk.

## 1. OPENING CEREMONIES

The meeting was called to order at 7:06 PM by Ward Six City Councilor Lance L. Davis. The City Council entered recess at 7:17 PM and returned at 7:18 PM.

The City Council entered recess at 7:45 PM and returned at 7:47 PM.

The City Council entered Executive Session at 8:05 PM and returned at 9:22PM.

1.1. Roll Call

Call of the Roll.

## (ID # 26-1370 ) RESULT: PLACED ON FILE

- Present: Ward Three City Councilor Ben Ewen-Campen
- City Councilor At Large Jon Link
- Ward Two City Councilor Jefferson Thomas (J.T.) Scott
- Ward Four City Councilor Jesse Clingan
- City Councilor At Large Kristen Strezo
- Ward Five City Councilor Naima Sait
- City Councilor At Large Ben Wheeler
- Ward Seven City Councilor Emily Hardt
- Ward One City Councilor Matthew McLaughlin
- City Councilor At Large Wilfred N. Mbah
- Ward Six City Councilor Lance L. Davis

1.2. Remembrances Remembrances.

## (ID # 26-1371 )

Councilor Mbah and Clingan requested a moment of silence in memory of Vijendra Kumar Pradhan.

Councilor Strezo requested a moment of silence in memory of Mary Bedard.

## RESULT: APPROVED

1.3. Minutes

Approval of the Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of July 9, (ID # 26-1372 ) 2026.

## RESULT: APPROVED

## 2. CITATIONS

## 3. PUBLIC HEARINGS

## 4. ORDERS, ORDINANCES, RESOLUTIONS AND MOTIONS OF MEMBERS

4.1. Resolution

By Councilor McLaughlin, Councilor Clingan, Councilor Davis, Councilor

(ID # 26-1217 ) Ewen-Campen, Councilor Hardt, Councilor Link, Councilor Mbah, Councilor Sait, Councilor Scott, Councilor Strezo and Councilor Wheeler

Recognizing the seriousness of myotonic dystrophy and expressing support for the designation of September 15, as ‘‘International Myotonic Dystrophy

- Awareness Day’’.

Discussed with item # 26-1366.

- Councilor McLaughlin sponsored Jim Nolan to speak. Mr. Nolan spoke

about being misdiagnosed for a number of years and noted that the symptoms are not the same for everyone. He mentioned that there is no

treatment or cure available to those afflicted with this illness and he thanked the Council for calling attention to this disease and for raising awareness about it.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.2. Resolution

By Councilor Clingan

(ID # 26-1359 ) In support of striking Encore Boston Harbor workers.

- Councilor Clingan spoke about visiting the picket line and stated that he
- stands with Encore workers, many of whom live in Somerville. Councilor

Clingan sponsored James Atkins and Fred Sanchez to speak. Mr. Atkins spoke about the difficulty of earning a decent wage at Encore and noted that there are 1,300 workers on strike. Mr. Sanchez Vasquez commented that the striking workers are asking to be paid according to the value of their work. Councilors Ewen-Campen, McLaughlin, Link, Scott, Mbah, Sait and Wheeler spoke in support of the workers.

## RESULT: APPROVED

4.3. Resolution

By Councilor Clingan

(ID # 26-1360 ) That the Director of Engineering and the Commissioner of Public Works

- discuss with the Committee on Public Utilities and Public Works the City’s

current requirements for restoration of streets following utility and other permitted excavations, including whether the City has the authority and ability to require full-lane, expanded, or curb-to-curb restoration on streets that have passed the five-year street opening moratorium but remain in good condition.

Discussed with item # 26-1361.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Sustainability and Infrastructure Committee

4.4. Resolution

By Councilor Clingan

(ID # 26-1361 ) That the Director of Engineering and Commissioner of Public Works

discuss with the Committee on Public Utilities and Public Works the feasibility of establishing a Street Preservation Offset Fee or similar

pavement-degradation fee, modeled on programs such as Cambridge’s, to help offset the City’s costs associated with utility and other excavations in public streets.

Discussed with item # 26-1360.

Councilor Clingan spoke about the city’s street opening policy and suggested that Somerville implement a program, like Cambridge has, whereby utility companies are charged a fee to assist with costs associated with excavations of public streets.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Sustainability and Infrastructure Committee

4.5. Resolution

By Councilor Clingan, Councilor Ewen-Campen, Councilor Link, Councilor

(ID # 26-1362 ) Hardt, Councilor Davis, Councilor Strezo, Councilor Sait, Councilor Mbah, Councilor Wheeler and Councilor Scott

That the Director of Engineering, the Commissioner of Public Works, and the Chief Procurement Officer discuss with the Committee on Public

Utilities and Public Works the City’s current practices for establishing, monitoring, and enforcing construction timelines for municipal projects, including the use of project milestones, completion deadlines, contractor

staffing levels, liquidated damages, and other tools to ensure that projects are completed in a timely manner.

Discussed with item # 26-1363.

Councilor Clingan spoke about the amount of time some projects take and he would like the city to be more proactive in the bidding process to ensure that work gets completed in a timely fashion.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Sustainability and Infrastructure Committee

4.6. Resolution

By Councilor Clingan

(ID # 26-1363 ) That the Director of Engineering, the Commissioner of Public Works, and the Chief Procurement Officer explore best practices used by other

municipalities and public agencies to encourage timely completion of public construction projects, including performance incentives, liquidated damages, milestone requirements, recovery schedules, and cost-plus-time or “A+B”

- bidding, and discuss which approaches could be appropriate for Somerville.

Discussed with item # 26-1362.

## RESULT: APPROVED AND SENT FOR DISCUSSION

FOLLOWUP: Sustainability and Infrastructure Committee

## 5. UNFINISHED BUSINESS

## 6. REPORTS OF COMMITTEES

6.A. FINANCE COMMITTEE

6.A.1. Committee Report Report of the Committee on Finance, meeting on September 3, 2026.

## (ID # 26-1355 )

- Councilor Wheeler reported that the Finance Committee approved 7 grant

acceptances and expenditures, 2 fund transfers, 2 fund appropriations, payment of 1 prior year invoice and the creation of 1 stabilization fund.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.2. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $65,000 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1219 ) match required, from the Mass Department of Mental Health to the Police

Department for operational funding for the Metro Boston Crisis Intervention Training and Technical Assistance Center.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.3. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $12,000 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1220 ) match required, from the Mass Department of Mental Health to the Police

- Department to partially fund the operation of the jail/arrest diversion
- program.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.4. Mayor's Request Requesting approval of a transfer of $315,000 from the Sewer Enterprise

(ID # 26-1226 ) Debt Service Account to the Morrison Avenue & Greater Davis Square Area

- Sewer Separation Design Capital Fund to fund required project
- expenditures.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.5. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to use available funds in the Police Salaries account in

(ID # 26-1234 ) the amount of $8,800 to fund Fiscal Year 2027 cost of living increases for

the Deputy Chief positions.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.6. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $284,700 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1241 ) match required, from the Massachusetts Gaming Commission to the Strategy and Development Department for Eastern Washington Street

- Transit Priority Project.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.7. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to pay a prior year invoice totaling $3,572 using

(ID # 26-1242 ) available funds in the Professional & Technical Services Account for the implementation of ArcGIS Urban module.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.8. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $85,933.60 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1243 ) match required, from the Boston Region Metropolitan Planning

Organization to the Mobility Division for the Bluebikes state of good repair equipment replacement.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.9. Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $366,729.25 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1248 ) match required, from the Metropolitan Area Planning Council to the Mobility Division, for new e-bikes, replacement batteries and two new

- docking stations as a part of the Bluebikes bikeshare system.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.10.Mayor's Request Requesting approval to create the Tufts Street Soil Project Stabilization

(ID # 26-1249 ) Fund and accept a payment to the Fund of $332,497 from the Unifirst

- Corporation to pay for cleanup and soil disposal costs associated with
- remediation work at 50 Tufts Street.

## RESULT: APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor Clingan, Ward Five City Councilor Sait,
- City Councilor At Large Wheeler, Ward Seven City
- Councilor Hardt, Ward One City Councilor McLaughlin,
- City Councilor At Large Mbah, and Ward Six City
- Councilor Davis
- ABSENT: City Councilor At Large Strezo

6.A.11.Mayor's Request Requesting approval to appropriate $332,497 from the Tufts Street Soil

(ID # 26-1250 ) Project Stabilization Fund for remediation efforts at 50 Tufts Street.

## RESULT: APPROVED

## AYE:

- Ward Three City Councilor Ewen-Campen, City Councilor
- At Large Link, Ward Two City Councilor Scott, Ward Four
- City Councilor Clingan, Ward Five City Councilor Sait,
- City Councilor At Large Wheeler, Ward Seven City
- Councilor Hardt, Ward One City Councilor McLaughlin,
- City Councilor At Large Mbah, and Ward Six City
- Councilor Davis
- ABSENT: City Councilor At Large Strezo

6.A.12.Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $187,200.00 Municipal

(ID # 26-1255 ) Vulnerability Preparedness Grant with no new match required, from the Executive Office of Energy and Environmental Affairs to the Public Space

- and Urban Forestry Division for the Green and Cool Somerville: Sustainable
- Sidewalk and Tree's project.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.13.Mayor's Request Requesting approval to accept and expend a $20,239 grant with no new

(ID # 26-1256 ) match required, from the United States Bureau of Justice Assistance to the Police Department for overtime related to the Fédération Internationale de

- Football Association In World Cup 2026 summer games.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.A.14.Mayor's Request Requesting approval of a transfer of $60,000 from the DPW-Admin Salaries

(ID # 26-1316 ) & Wages Temp Account to the DPW-Admin Professional & Technical

Services Account to support temporary clerical staffing.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.B. LAND USE COMMITTEE

6.B.1. Committee Report Report of the Committee on Land Use, meeting on September 3, 2026.

## (ID # 26-1356 )

- Councilor Ewen-Campen reported that the Land Use Committee approved

the Urban Center Housing Tax Increment Financing (UCH-TIF) Zone, Plan, and Form of Agreement for Assembly Square and East Somerville as well as

- an amendment to Section 2.1.1 of the Zoning Ordinance regarding Homeless
- Shelters.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.B.2. Mayor's Request Requesting approval of the Urban Center Housing Tax Increment Financing

(ID # 26-0746 ) (UCH-TIF) Zone, Plan, and Form of Agreement for Assembly Square and East Somerville.

## RESULT: APPROVED AYE:

- City Councilor At Large Wheeler, Ward Seven City

6.B.3. Zoning Ordinance By Councilor Davis, Councilor Ewen-Campen, Councilor Clingan, (ID # 26-0835 ) Councilor Link, Councilor Mbah, Councilor Hardt, Councilor Sait and Councilor Wheeler

Proposing an amendment to Section 2.1.1 of the Zoning Ordinance regarding Homeless Shelters.

## RESULT: ORDINANCE ORDAINED AS AMENDED AYE:

- Ward Three City Councilor Ewen-Campen, City Councilor
- At Large Link, Ward Two City Councilor Scott, Ward Four

- City Councilor At Large Wheeler, Ward Seven City
- Councilor Hardt, Ward One City Councilor McLaughlin,
- City Councilor At Large Mbah, and Ward Six City

6.C. SCHOOL BUILDING FACILITIES AND MAINTENANCE COMMITTEE

6.C.1. Committee Report Report of the Committee on School Building Facilities and Maintenance, (ID # 26-1357 ) meeting on September 8, 2026.

Councilor Link reported that the committee discussed custodial staffing, rodent control, temperature control, updates on the Winter Hill School plan, re-use possibilities for the Cummings School building and seeking space for a teen center.

## RESULT: APPROVED

6.C.2. Resolution

By Councilor Link and Councilor Wheeler

(ID # 26-0063 ) That the Commissioner of Public Works and the Director of Engineering

explore the feasibility of establishing a teen center at the Cummings School, accessible via School Street, considering current building uses and provide this Council with an analysis on space availability, operational

- considerations, community impacts, and potential next steps.

## RESULT: WORK COMPLETED

6.C.3. Order

By Councilor Link and Councilor McLaughlin

(ID # 26-0839 ) That the Commissioner of Public Works provide an update to this Council

- on improvements made to custodial staffing at the East Somerville
- Community School.

## RESULT: WORK COMPLETED

6.C.4. Resolution

By Councilor Hardt

(ID # 26-1022 ) Recognizing and expressing appreciation to the Department of Public

- Works, the Department of Health and Human Services Division of Public

Health, and the Inspectional Services Department for their work in addressing rodent issues at the West Somerville Neighborhood School.

## RESULT: WORK COMPLETED

## 7. COMMUNICATIONS OF THE MAYOR

7.1. Mayor's Request Requesting that this Council convene in Executive Session to receive an

(ID # 26-1364 ) update on collective bargaining negotiations.

- The Council voted to enter into Executive Session to discuss this matter
- after being advised by Assistant City Solicitor/Labor Counsel Matthew
- Sirigu that the item to be discussed meets the criteria set forth in the
- Massachusetts Open Meeting Law.

- The regular meeting was adjourned at 8:05 PM and the members moved into
- Executive Session.

- The regular meeting was reconvened 9:22 PM. President Davis announced

that no votes were taken in Executive Session, other than the vote to adjourn.

## RESULT: APPROVED

7.2. Mayor's Request Requesting ordainment of an amendment to Sections 3.2.17, 4.1.15, 4.2.15, (ID # 26-1258 ) 4.3.15, 4.4.15, 5.1.16, 6.1.13, 6.2.14, 6.3.13, 6.4.16, 6.5.13 of the Somerville

Zoning Ordinance to correct parking maximums.

President Davis waived the readings of items 7.2 and 7.4 through 7.7 and referred them to the Land Use Committee.

- Councilor Wheeler asked if these items are being put forth by the Planning

and Zoning Department. Councilor Ewen-Campen stated that these items will be referred to the Land Use Committee for a public hearing on October

- 1st, at which time each item will be explained in detail. Director of

Intergovernmental Affairs, Amanda Nagim-Williams, explained that a majority of these items are to rectify omissions or to clear up language.

7.21. Mayor's

Conveying an update on Civilian Oversight.

Communication

## (ID # 26-1353 )

- Jon Hillman, Public Safety for All Project Manager, provided a brief
- presentation on the development of Somerville’s Civilian Oversight

Initiative. The initiative has evolved over more than two decades, beginning with calls from the Human Rights Commission in the early 2000s and gaining momentum in 2020, when the City declared systemic racism a

public health emergency. At that time, 81% of surveyed residents expressed support for civilian oversight. Recommendations from community groups

- and the City Council in 2021 led to the creation of a two-year Civilian

Oversight Task Force process, which concluded in 2025 with detailed guidance regarding the mission, role, composition, and implementation of a

civilian oversight body. The City is currently reviewing key resources, including the Task Force Report, Racial and Social Justice workshops, City

Council analyses, and community policy recommendations. The City is also considering Peace Officer Standards and Training Commission

requirements, collective bargaining considerations, policy development steps, and civilian oversight models used in other municipalities. Upcoming milestones include a September 10 overview and bargaining update, a

- September 24 administration update, a tentative September 29 Legislative
- Matters discussion, and an October public hearing.

- The item was laid on the table to allow item #26-1364, a request to enter

into Executive Session, to be taken up. Following the Executive Session, the item was removed from the table for further discussion.

- Councilor Ewen-Campen stated that the City needs meaningful civilian

oversight of the Police Department, including a significant role in investigations and disciplinary matters. He also noted that an oversight body should have the ability to obtain information and issue subpoenas, as well as make decisions and recommendations based on the information it collects.

Councilor Scott noted that civilian oversight has been sought by both the City Council and residents for many years and cautioned against adopting

policies that have not been effective in other communities. Councilor Sait stated that the civilian oversight body should have a strong role in

disciplinary matters, the ability to conduct parallel investigations into complaints, and access to relevant information and video footage.

- Councilor Hardt asked whether all pertinent documents related to civilian

oversight could be centralized to make the information easier for the public to access. Mr. Hillman stated that the documents are publicly available and that his department would work to make them available in one location, although he could not provide a specific timeline. President Davis asked to be informed of any obstacles that could prevent the documents from being

centralized. Councilor Wheeler stated that civilian oversight should include ongoing review of police policies and practices, have access to funding for investigative support, and provide regular opportunities for collaboration

- between the oversight body and the Police Department.

- Councilor Mbah assumed the Chair to allow President Davis to speak on the
- item. Councilor Davis reiterated several points raised by the other

Councilors and noted that civilian oversight bodies in other municipalities have, in some cases, not functioned as intended because they lacked

sufficient authority or resources. He also stated that, in addition to the responsibilities discussed, there should be a clear process governing when

and how information collected by the civilian oversight body would be released to the public. Councilor Davis encouraged members of the public to share their concerns and experiences with the City Council so that their

input could be considered in developing the structure of the civilian oversight body.
